facts.value: Bioscience is the branch of the sciences concerned with living organisms, from microorganisms to towering trees and gigantic whales. Within this incredibly broad branch of the sciences, there are a number of smaller branches focused on specific issues which pertain to living organisms.

This branch of scientific inquiry is extremely important. Bioscience is the foundation of many other schools of scientific inquiry, ranging from medicine to agronomy, and new discoveries in this field are being made every day.

Bioscience developed into a serious line of scientific inquiry in the 19th century, when people began to explore the natural world from a scientific perspective. However, people have been studying and practicing bioscience for centuries.
Bioscientists study the nature of living organisms, their behavior, their evolutionary history, and their potential uses.

Depending on the subset of bioscience a researcher is involved with, they may spend time at the laboratory bench probing into the chemical composition of living organisms, or time in the field studying wild animals in situ.
Bioscience intersects with a number of other scientific branches, such as chemistry and physics.
A bioscientist can be described by the type of organisms studied, such as zoologists, botanists, and microbiologists.
Bioscience may also be referred to as biology or life science.
People who work in the field of bioscience typically have extensive education in the sciences, with additional study in the field they have chosen.
